title.title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss
title.subtitle: Claim: the chromatic height lost from $H$- to $G$-fixed points equals the shortest cyclic subnormal chain

plain: Climbing up through a group loses some 'resolution'; the loss is exactly the number of simple steps you climb

beats.text: Schematically: $H \lhd H_1 \lhd H_2 \lhd G$, every quotient cyclic; $\ell_{\mathrm{cyc}}$ is the shortest length
$r_n(G,H)$: the chromatic height lost passing from $H$- to $G$-fixed points
The chain length was an upper bound; the claim is that it is exact

steps: Chains of cyclic steps already gave an upper bound on the loss
New finite spectra show that much loss really happens
Lower meets upper: the loss equals the chain length

achievement.label: Kuhn–Lloyd's cautious hope (chromatic Smith theory)
statement: r_n(G,H) = \ell_{\mathrm{cyc}}(H,G) \ \text{ for every finite } p\text{-group } G
achievement.context: Before: abelian $G$, where the loss is the rank of $G/H$ (2019), and some central extensions (Kuhn–Lloyd)
achievement.note: Completes the Balmer-spectrum topology for finite $p$-groups, if correct

verify.detail: Manuscript only: 30 pages, a technical result
verify.ourCheck: We read the proof outline; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Climb from H to G by cyclic steps. How much height is lost?
The chain bounds the loss; new examples show the bound is reached.
Claimed: the loss equals the shortest chain.

sources.quote: equals the least length of a subnormal chain from H to G with cyclic quotients.
(2019) solved abelian G (loss = rank of G/H); Kuhn-Lloyd proved equality for central extensions of elementary abelian by C_2 and expressed 'cautious hope'
30 pages; completes the Balmer spectrum topology for p-groups if correct.
The upper bound by cyclic subnormal chains was known
